useCases.title: Event-specific validation
useCases.scenario: Apply different rules when editing versus leaving the field.

keyPoints: A field can validate immediately with synchronous rules or perform asynchronous checks such as server/API validation.
Choose validator names that match the field event, including change and blur asynchronous checks.
For blur validation, the synchronous rule executes before the asynchronous rule by default.
Set asyncDebounceMs on the field to delay asynchronous validation and reduce repeated checks.
Validators can belong directly to an individual field, rather than requiring form-level rules.
gotchas: By default, the asynchronous validator runs only after its synchronous counterpart succeeds; use asyncAlways when it must run despite synchronous errors.
A field-level asyncDebounceMs applies to every asynchronous validation unless a specific validator override is supplied.
Use an event-specific debounce such as onChangeAsyncDebounceMs when different async triggers need different delays.

Hooks::form.Field.sourceTitle: Basic Concepts and Terminology | TanStack Form React Docs
Hooks::form.Field.summary: form.Field binds one form value to UI through a render prop. The callback receives the field API, including its state and event handlers, so field-specific updates do not require rendering the whole form.
Hooks::form.Field.explanation: In React, render form.Field with a name matching a default-value key. Its children render prop receives the field API, which exposes the current value, name, blur handler, and change handler; reading field.state keeps the field-specific UI connected to that field.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Field path matching a key in the form's default values.

parameters.name: children
parameters.description: Render prop receiving the field object.

parameters.name: validators
parameters.description: Optional field-specific validation configuration.

Hooks::form.Field.returns: A rendered field whose render prop receives the field API.

example.title: Binding an input with form.Field
example.explanation: Creates a typed field binding whose render prop receives the field API and connects an input to its value and event handlers.

useCases.title: Single-control forms
useCases.scenario: Bind a text, checkbox, or similar single input to one form value.

useCases.title: Field-local feedback
useCases.scenario: Render a value, validation result, or error beside only the relevant control.

useCases.title: Field-specific validation
useCases.scenario: Attach validation rules to one field rather than the complete form.

interview.question: What does form.Field provide?
interview.answer: form.Field creates a field for one form value. Its name identifies the value, and its children render prop receives the field object used to connect the input.
interview.followUp: How would you display field-specific validation? Use the field object's state metadata and render its errors alongside the input.

interview.question: How is an input connected to a field?
interview.answer: The field object exposes state and event methods. A controlled input commonly reads field.state.value, calls field.handleChange when its value changes, and calls field.handleBlur on blur.
interview.followUp: Why bind these handlers instead of updating local state? They keep the value and field lifecycle within TanStack Form's field state.

interview.question: What state is available for a field?
interview.answer: Each field has independent state containing its current value, validation status, errors, and other metadata. Rendering through the field's callback lets the component consume that field-specific state.
interview.followUp: How can validation be attached? Pass field-specific validators to form.Field, including synchronous or asynchronous validation functions.

keyPoints: Use one Field for a single input-like value, including text controls and checkboxes.
The form instance supplies the Field component used to declare individual bindings.
The name identifies which default-value entry the field controls.
The render prop receives the field API, allowing the input markup to remain colocated with its binding logic.
Field state is scoped per field and includes value, validation, errors, and metadata.
Read field.state inside the render prop to render field-specific UI.
gotchas: The name must correspond to a key in the form's defaultValues; mismatches are not valid field bindings.
The field UI belongs inside the children render prop so it can use the supplied field object.

Hooks::form.Subscribe.summary: form.Subscribe selectively re-renders a UI region when the form-state value returned by its selector changes. It is intended for reactive UI updates, while useSelector is preferred for logic-level reactivity.
Hooks::form.Subscribe.explanation: Use form.Subscribe inside the UI when a rendered region depends on form state. Its selector chooses the value to observe, and the child function receives that selected value; changes re-render the Subscribe region without causing a component-level re-render.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: Function that selects the form-state value or structure to observe.

parameters.name: children
parameters.description: Render function receiving the selected value.

Hooks::form.Subscribe.returns: A rendered UI region produced by the children function.

example.title: Subscribe to submit readiness
example.explanation: This React component renders a submit button from the form's current canSubmit state. Only the Subscribe region updates when that selected value changes.

useCases.title: Reactive submit controls
useCases.scenario: A submit button needs to enable or disable itself from state.canSubmit.

useCases.title: Conditional form UI
useCases.scenario: A section should appear or disappear according to a field value.

useCases.title: Isolated status rendering
useCases.scenario: A small status display should reflect selected form state without updating the parent component.

interview.question: What problem does form.Subscribe solve?
interview.answer: form.Subscribe is a component for reacting to form state in rendered UI. Its selector selects the relevant state, and its child receives that selection.
interview.followUp: How does it improve rendering? Only the Subscribe region re-renders when the selected value changes, rather than the containing component.

interview.question: What is the purpose of the selector?
interview.answer: The selector determines which form-state value the component observes. For example, selecting state.values.firstName lets the UI react only to that field value.
interview.followUp: How can multiple values be observed? Return an object or array containing the needed state values, then consume that selected structure in the child.

interview.question: When should you choose form.Subscribe instead of useSelector?
interview.answer: Use form.Subscribe when form-state changes should directly update rendered UI, such as showing or hiding UI or controlling a submit button. useSelector is better when reactivity is needed in logic.
interview.followUp: Why should the selector stay focused? A narrow selection limits updates to the state that the UI actually needs.

keyPoints: Use it for UI that depends on form state, such as conditionally displaying an element.
Reactive form values are accessed through a subscription mechanism, with form.Subscribe being the UI-oriented option.
Updates are isolated to the Subscribe region rather than re-rendering the entire component.
A field's value can drive conditional rendering through the selector and child renderer.
Choose between the two APIs according to whether the subscription serves rendered UI or component logic.
gotchas: Do not expect changing subscribed state to re-render the surrounding component; only the Subscribe component updates.
For reactive UI, prefer form.Subscribe; use useSelector when the reactivity is needed in component logic.

Hooks::useField.summary: A React hook for managing one TanStack Form field. It returns that field’s FieldApi so a component can read state, update the value, run field-level validation, and inspect metadata.
Hooks::useField.explanation: In React, call useField with a form instance, a field name, and optional field configuration. The hook returns a FieldApi that exposes the field's reactive state, event handlers, validation behavior, metadata, and mutation methods, letting a component render and update one field independently.
Hooks::useField.syntax: useField<TParentData, TName, TData, TOnMount, TOnChange, TOnChangeAsync, TOnBlur, TOnBlurAsync, TOnSubmit, TOnSubmitAsync, TOnDynamic, TOnDynamicAsync, TFormOnMount, TFormOnChange, TFormOnChangeAsync, TFormOnBlur, TFormOnBlurAsync, TFormOnSubmit, TFormOnSubmitAsync, TFormOnDynamic, TFormOnDynamicAsync, TFormOnServer, TPatentSubmitMeta>(opts): FieldApi<TParentData, TName, TData, TOnMount, TOnChange, TOnChangeAsync, TOnBlur, TOnBlurAsync, TOnSubmit, TOnSubmitAsync, TOnDynamic, TOnDynamicAsync, TFormOnMount, TFormOnChange, TFormOnChangeAsync, TFormOnBlur, TFormOnBlurAsync, TFormOnSubmit, TFormOnSubmitAsync, TFormOnDynamic, TFormOnDynamicAsync, TFormOnServer, TPatentSubmitMeta>

parameters.name: opts
parameters.type: UseFieldOptions<TParentData, TName, TData, TOnMount, TOnChange, TOnChangeAsync, TOnBlur, TOnBlurAsync, TOnSubmit, TOnSubmitAsync, TOnDynamic, TOnDynamicAsync, TFormOnMount, TFormOnChange, TFormOnChang
parameters.description: Options used to configure and identify the field, represented by the generic UseFieldOptions type.

Hooks::useField.returns: The FieldApi instance for the specified field.

example.title: A standalone validated field
example.explanation: Creates a field API for email, binds its value and event handlers to an input, and displays validation errors.

useCases.title: Build a reusable field control
useCases.scenario: A custom input component needs direct access to one field’s value, handlers, and metadata.

useCases.title: Attach field-level validation
useCases.scenario: A field has rules that should run on change, blur, mount, submit, or dynamic conditions.

useCases.title: Localize field interaction
useCases.scenario: A component should update a field without rendering the complete form API.

interview.question: What does useField do, and what does it return?
interview.answer: useField is a hook for managing a field in a form. It returns the FieldApi instance for the specified field, which the component can use to read state and handle field interactions.
interview.followUp: How can a component avoid manually calling useField? Use the Field component, which accepts field options and a render function and uses useField internally.

interview.question: What is the shape of the useField call?
interview.answer: Pass an options object to useField. The generic signature shows that the options can describe the parent form data, field name and data, field-level lifecycle validators, form-level validators, and submit metadata.
interview.followUp: Which result type should callers expect? The React hook returns FieldApi parameterized by the supplied field and validator types.

interview.question: How does useField support field-specific validation?
interview.answer: A field can define validators for mount, change, asynchronous change, blur, asynchronous blur, submit, asynchronous submit, dynamic validation, and asynchronous dynamic validation. These options let validation be attached to the field rather than only to the whole form.
interview.followUp: What should a UI render for validation feedback? Read the returned field API's state and metadata, then render the relevant errors or status.

keyPoints: useField creates the field-management object used by a component.
The return value is a FieldApi for the named field.
Its generic signature carries parent-data, field-name, field-data, and validator-related types through the API.
The field configuration can represent synchronous and asynchronous change, blur, and submit validation.
The signature also includes dynamic field validation and form-level lifecycle validation types.

Hooks::useStore with a form selector.summary: useStore subscribes a component to a selected slice of a TanStack Form store, such as canSubmit, isDirty, or errors. It is deprecated; useSelector provides the current API with the same arguments.
Hooks::useStore with a form selector.explanation: In React, useStore reads from a store-like source and optionally applies a selector to return a selected form-state value. The current documentation marks it as a deprecated alias for useSelector, so new code should use useSelector with the same source, selector, and optional comparison arguments.
Hooks::useStore with a form selector.syntax: const useStore: <TSource, TSelected>(source, selector?, compare?) => TSelected;

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The store-like source whose snapshot is read.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: Optional function receiving the source snapshot and returning the subscribed selection.

parameters.name: compare
parameters.description: Optional equality function comparing two selected values.

example.title: Subscribe to canSubmit
example.explanation: Selects only the submission-readiness flag, so the component reacts when that selected value changes.

useCases.title: Submit-state UI
useCases.scenario: Enable or disable a submit control based on form readiness.

useCases.title: Error presentation
useCases.scenario: Show validation feedback when the selected error state changes.

useCases.title: Conditional form logic
useCases.scenario: Drive conditional sections from a selected dirty or value state.

interview.question: What does useStore return and how can it target form state?
interview.answer: useStore accepts a source, an optional selector, and an optional comparison function, then returns the selected value. For form state, the selector can return a narrow value such as state.canSubmit.
interview.followUp: Why select a slice instead of omitting the selector? The documentation warns that omitting it can cause re-renders whenever any form-state value changes.

interview.question: How does a form selector limit the subscribed state?
interview.answer: The selector receives the source snapshot and returns TSelected. A component can therefore subscribe to values, errors, or status flags without reading the entire form state.
interview.followUp: How should new code express this subscription? Use useSelector with the same arguments, because useStore is deprecated.

interview.question: When would the compare argument matter?
interview.answer: The optional compare argument receives the previous and next selected values and returns a boolean. It can define equality behavior for selected results when the default comparison is not sufficient.
interview.followUp: What is the practical caution with a selector that returns an aggregate value? Keep the selection focused, because a changed aggregate result can trigger the component to re-render.

keyPoints: The hook is generic over the source and selected result, and accepts optional selector and comparison arguments.
The selector transforms a source snapshot into the value exposed to the component.
The optional compare function receives two selected values and determines whether they compare equally.
The documented usage passes a store and selects one property from its state.
gotchas: useStore is deprecated; prefer useSelector for new code.
The documented replacement is useSelector.

Hooks::useTransform and mergeForm.summary: Use useTransform with mergeForm to fold server-returned form state into the current client form. Include the returned state in the dependency list so the merge updates after submissions or server loads.
Hooks::useTransform and mergeForm.explanation: useTransform supplies a form transformation, while mergeForm applies server-returned form state to the existing client form. Put the merge in the transform and include the server state in the dependency list so a new submission result is incorporated when it arrives.

parameters.name: baseForm
parameters.description: The current client form passed to the transformation callback.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Form state returned by the server or another external source to merge into the base form.

parameters.name: useTransform callback
parameters.description: A callback that receives the base form and returns the transformed form.

parameters.name: dependencies
parameters.description: Values that cause the transform to be recalculated when they change.

Hooks::useTransform and mergeForm.returns: mergeForm returns a FormApi with the supplied state merged into the base form; useTransform provides the transformed form for useForm.

example.title: Merge returned server state into a form
example.explanation: Pass the latest server state as a dependency so the transform merges it into the client form when that state changes.

useCases.title: React server actions
useCases.scenario: A server action returns validation errors or updated form state after submit.

useCases.title: TanStack Start loader data
useCases.scenario: A route loader provides initial or refreshed form state from the server.

useCases.title: Remix action data
useCases.scenario: A framework action hook exposes the latest submission result to the client.

interview.question: How do useTransform and mergeForm work together?
interview.answer: useTransform lets the form derive a transformed FormApi from a base form. In this pattern, the transform callback calls mergeForm with the base form and server state, while the dependency array makes the transformation respond to new state.
interview.followUp: Why include server state in the dependency array? Because the transform needs to be recalculated when a new submission result arrives; otherwise the form can retain the prior merged result.

interview.question: What does mergeForm return?
interview.answer: mergeForm takes a base form and a form state, then returns a FormApi containing the merged result. This lets server-returned values or errors be incorporated without constructing a separate client form.
interview.followUp: What should the merge target be? The current base form returned to the transform callback, not a stale form instance.

interview.question: How should returned server state be wired into a React form?
interview.answer: Use the server state in the transform's dependency list: useTransform((baseForm) => mergeForm(baseForm, state), [state]). The official example obtains state from loader data and merges it into the form.
interview.followUp: How can the same approach support an action response? Replace loader state with action data and merge that value whenever it changes.

keyPoints: mergeForm accepts the existing base form plus returned form state and produces a FormApi.
Configure the merge through useForm's transform option and list the incoming state as a dependency.
The pattern is suitable for server actions because their returned state can be merged into the client form.
The same transform pattern works with framework-provided action data.
gotchas: The merged state must come from the server action's returned state; useTransform is the bridge that applies it to the client form.

Submission & integration::canSubmit and.summary: Derive submit controls from TanStack Form state: canSubmit reflects whether submission is currently allowed, while isSubmitting reflects active submission. Subscribe to them instead of maintaining a separate loading flag.
Submission & integration::canSubmit and.explanation: TanStack Form exposes canSubmit and isSubmitting through form state. Subscribe to both values, disable submission when canSubmit is false, and show progress while isSubmitting is true; await asynchronous work in onSubmit so the submitting state ends when that work finishes.
Submission & integration::canSubmit and.returns: canSubmit and isSubmitting are form-state booleans used to derive submission controls.

example.title: Derive submit-button state from the form
example.explanation: Subscribes to the two form-state values so the button reflects validity and submission progress without a separate loading flag.

useCases.title: Guard invalid submissions
useCases.scenario: Disable a submit button when validation currently prevents submission.

useCases.title: Display submission progress
useCases.scenario: Show a progress label or indicator during asynchronous submission.

useCases.title: Combine validity with pristine state
useCases.scenario: Prevent submission until the user has interacted with the form.

keyPoints: canSubmit is derived from the current form state and indicates whether submission is allowed.
isSubmitting indicates that submission is in progress after handleSubmit has been called.
isSubmitting returns to false when validation fails or the onSubmit function finishes.
gotchas: Await asynchronous work inside onSubmit; otherwise isSubmitting can reset before the operation actually completes.

Submission & integration::Framework adap.summary: Use the adapter package for your UI framework to connect TanStack Form to React, Vue, Solid, Angular, and other supported runtimes. The framework-specific binding lets the shared form model remain the basis for state, validation, and submission.
Submission & integration::Framework adap.explanation: TanStack Form keeps form state and behavior framework-agnostic, while adapter packages provide framework-specific bindings. Select the package matching the UI runtime—for example, @tanstack/react-form, @tanstack/vue-form, @tanstack/solid-form, or @tanstack/angular-form—then use that framework's APIs without changing the underlying form model.

example.title: Use a framework adapter
example.explanation: The React adapter exposes the shared form model through React-oriented APIs such as useForm and form.Field. The same core form concepts can be connected through the corresponding adapter package for another supported framework.

useCases.title: React form integration
useCases.scenario: A React application needs typed form state and submission handling without adopting a UI component library.

useCases.title: Cross-framework form architecture
useCases.scenario: A team shares form behavior across applications built with different UI frameworks.

useCases.title: Non-React integration
useCases.scenario: A project uses Vue, Solid, or Angular and needs TanStack Form’s form-management model.

interview.question: What is a TanStack Form framework adapter?
interview.answer: The adapter is the framework-specific package that connects TanStack Form to a UI runtime. For example, React uses @tanstack/react-form, while Vue, Angular, and Solid use their corresponding packages.
interview.followUp: How would you preserve portability when moving from React to Vue? Keep the form model, values, validation, and submission behavior conceptually the same, then replace the framework binding and its package with the Vue adapter.

interview.question: How do you select the correct adapter?
interview.answer: Choose the adapter associated with the application’s framework: @tanstack/react-form, @tanstack/vue-form, @tanstack/angular-form, or @tanstack/solid-form. The framework page also lists adapters for Preact, Svelte, and Lit.
interview.followUp: What should you do if the target framework is not listed? The page invites developers to discuss implementation details and support for creating another adapter.

interview.question: How is a React adapter used in a form?
interview.answer: The React example imports useForm from @tanstack/react-form, creates a form with defaultValues and onSubmit, and renders it through React JSX. Submission is wired by preventing the browser event and calling form.handleSubmit().
interview.followUp: Why is preventing the native submit event necessary in this example? It stops the browser’s default navigation so TanStack Form can run its configured submission handler instead.

keyPoints: TanStack Form supports multiple UI frameworks through separate adapter packages.
Lit has a dedicated adapter package, @tanstack/lit-form.
The documentation welcomes contributions or discussion around building additional framework adapters.
gotchas: Install the adapter package that matches the framework; the documentation does not describe one universal adapter package.

Submission & integration::Reset and clea.summary: Reset a TanStack Form to its default values or provide replacement values. By default, replacement values become the new reset baseline; preserve the old baseline with updateDefaultValues: false.
Submission & integration::Reset and clea.explanation: TanStack Form uses defaultValues as the reset baseline. Calling reset() restores those values and clears form state, while reset(values) replaces the current values and, by default, establishes those values as the new baseline. Use updateDefaultValues: false when supplying values but retaining the previous baseline.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Optional replacement values for the form; when provided, they become current values and normally the new default baseline.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Optional reset configuration. Set updateDefaultValues to false to preserve the existing defaultValues baseline.

Submission & integration::Reset and clea.returns: Resets form values, metadata, validation state, and mounted fields; pending validation or submission results are discarded.

example.title: Reset a form to its defaults
example.explanation: A reset button calls TanStack Form's reset method and returns the form to its current default values.

useCases.title: Restore defaults
useCases.scenario: Discarding edits and returning an editor to its configured starting data.

useCases.title: Apply external data
useCases.scenario: Loading a saved draft or freshly fetched record into the active form.

useCases.title: Preserve baseline
useCases.scenario: Applying temporary values while keeping the original reset and comparison baseline.

interview.question: What does reset() restore?
interview.answer: defaultValues provide the initial data shape and the baseline used by reset(). Calling reset() restores that baseline and resets form metadata, validation state, and mounted fields.
interview.followUp: How can a saved draft be displayed without making it the new baseline? Call reset(savedDraft, { updateDefaultValues: false }); subsequent reset() calls still restore the earlier defaults.

interview.question: What is the effect of reset(values)?
interview.answer: reset(values) replaces the current values and, by default, also updates defaultValues. Future reset() calls therefore return to the supplied values.
interview.followUp: What happens if updateDefaultValues is false? The supplied values become current, but the existing defaults remain the comparison and reset baseline.

interview.question: How should a reset button be wired?
interview.answer: A type="reset" button invokes the browser's native reset behavior as well as the handler. Prevent the default event before calling form.reset(), or use type="button" instead.
interview.followUp: Why is the native behavior risky? It can restore controls such as select elements to their HTML initial values, producing an unexpected result.

keyPoints: A form reset is broader than changing inputs: it clears values and associated form state.
Pending validation or submission results are thrown away when reset runs.
Supplying reset values is useful for applying newly loaded or saved backend data immediately.
Use updateDefaultValues: false to apply temporary current values without changing the established defaults.
gotchas: A native button with type="reset" can also trigger the browser's reset behavior. Prevent the event before calling form.reset(), or use type="button".
Do not assume reset() means empty values: it returns to the current defaultValues. Define empty defaults when an empty reset is required.
Passing values changes the reset baseline by default; use the options form when that should not happen.

Validation::Async validators.sourceTitle: Form and Field Validation | TanStack Form React Docs
Validation::Async validators.summary: TanStack Form supports async validators for server-backed checks such as username availability. Debounce them to limit requests; failed async validation produces errors that prevent a valid form submission.
Validation::Async validators.explanation: TanStack Form supports asynchronous validators for network-backed checks. Configure an async validator such as onDynamicAsync or a field-level onChangeAsync, optionally pair it with an async debounce setting, and return an error object or message when the server rejects the value; successful validation returns undefined. Async validation state is tracked by the form and participates in submission validation.
Validation::Async validators.syntax:
validators: { onChangeAsync: async ({ value }) => { return condition ? 'error' : undefined } }
asyncDebounceMs: 500

parameters.name: { value }
parameters.description: The validation callback context, including the current value used by the asynchronous validator.

parameters.name: asyncDebounceMs
parameters.description: Milliseconds to wait before invoking asynchronous validation after its trigger fires.

parameters.name: onChangeAsyncDebounceMs
parameters.description: Milliseconds to wait before invoking a specific asynchronous trigger, such as onChangeAsync.

Validation::Async validators.returns: Return undefined when the value passes; return a string for a field error or an object mapping field names to errors for form-level validation.

example.title: Debounced username availability validation
example.explanation: The form runs an asynchronous dynamic validator after a 500 ms debounce. It checks the username through an API and returns a field error when unavailable; returning undefined marks it valid. Form submission is handled through the form API, so validation runs before submission proceeds.

useCases.title: Availability checks
useCases.scenario: A username or email must be checked against records that already exist on the server.

useCases.title: Debounced remote validation
useCases.scenario: Typing should not issue a request for every keystroke.

useCases.title: Form-level async rules
useCases.scenario: A rule depends on several fields or the complete form value.

interview.question: How do you implement server-backed validation in TanStack Form?
interview.answer: Use an async validator such as onChangeAsync, onBlurAsync, or onDynamicAsync. It receives the current value, performs the asynchronous operation, and returns an error when invalid or undefined when valid.
interview.followUp: How would you reduce server traffic while typing? Add an async debounce setting, such as onDynamicAsyncDebounceMs or asyncDebounceMs, so calls wait for a quiet period.

interview.question: How do you debounce asynchronous validation?
interview.answer: Set a debounce duration alongside the asynchronous validator. For a field, asyncDebounceMs applies a default delay to async calls, while a trigger-specific setting such as onChangeAsyncDebounceMs can override it.
interview.followUp: How can blur and change validation use different delays? Configure the shared field debounce and override the change or blur-specific debounce as needed.

interview.question: What is the execution order between sync and async validators?
interview.answer: Synchronous and asynchronous validators can coexist. The synchronous validator runs first for the same trigger, and the asynchronous validator runs only when the synchronous check succeeds unless asyncAlways is enabled.
interview.followUp: What happens if the synchronous check fails but the server check is still required? Set asyncAlways to true so the asynchronous validator runs regardless.

keyPoints: Use asynchronous validation when correctness depends on a server or another operation that does not complete immediately.
Choose an async trigger based on the user interaction that should initiate the remote check, such as change or blur.
Debouncing is configured directly on the form field instead of requiring a separate timing wrapper around the validator.
A field-level asyncDebounceMs value delays all asynchronous validations for that field by the configured interval.
Place async validation on an individual field or on the complete form when the rule depends on multiple values.
gotchas: When synchronous and asynchronous validators share an event, the synchronous validator runs first; the async validator is skipped if it fails.
Set asyncAlways to true when the asynchronous check must run even after synchronous validation fails.
A validator-specific debounce overrides the field-level debounce, so different async triggers can use different delays.

Validation::Error mapping.sourceTitle: Form and Field Validation | TanStack Form React Docs
Validation::Error mapping.summary: Map validation failures to field metadata and render them beside the responsible input. Use errors for all current messages or errorMap for a message from a specific validation phase.
Validation::Error mapping.explanation: TanStack Form exposes field validation failures through metadata. Read the combined errors from field.state.meta.errors, or select an error by validation phase through field.state.meta.errorMap; form-level validators can also set errors on individual fields.

example.title: Display a server failure on one field
example.explanation: A server response is placed in the field's submit error map, then rendered from that field's metadata.

useCases.title: Show a server failure beside the email field
useCases.scenario: A server rejects an email as already registered after submission.

useCases.title: Assign cross-field validation to the responsible field
useCases.scenario: A form validator checks multiple related fields and identifies one invalid value.

useCases.title: Select an error by validation phase
useCases.scenario: The interface needs different messages for live, blur, and submit validation.

interview.question: How can a field's validation errors be read?
interview.answer: Use field.state.meta.errors when the UI should show all current failures for a field. Use field.state.meta.errorMap when the UI needs the failure associated with a particular validation phase.
interview.followUp: How do you retain the origin of errors? Preserve the separate validation sources instead of relying only on the flattened errors array.

interview.question: When is errorMap preferable to errors?
interview.answer: The field metadata exposes errorMap entries keyed by validation timing, such as onChange, onBlur, or onSubmit. This lets the UI choose the appropriate message for the interaction that produced it.
interview.followUp: What type should an errorMap entry have? It should match the value returned by that corresponding validator.

interview.question: How can form-level validation target a specific field?
interview.answer: Errors can be assigned to fields from the form's validators, allowing a form-level check, including a server result, to target the field that caused the failure. The field then exposes that result through its metadata.
interview.followUp: How should a form-wide failure be displayed? Read the form-level error map rather than attaching it to an unrelated field.

keyPoints: A validator can report failure by returning an error message string.
Returned field errors are exposed through the field's metadata errors array.
The errors array can contain multiple simultaneous failures.
Use errorMap to choose errors by validation phase instead of using the combined list.
The error map supports selecting a particular validation result for display.
Form-level validators can place failures on the individual fields responsible for them.
gotchas: The combined errors array does not preserve which validation source produced each error unless source-specific handling is enabled.
Keep error values compatible with the validator associated with the selected errorMap key.

Validation::Field validators.summary: Field validators check one field at a chosen validation event and return an error message when its value is invalid. The message is exposed through the field's error state for rendering.
Validation::Field validators.explanation: A field validator is a callback attached to a field validation event such as onChange or onBlur. TanStack Form supplies the current value and field API; return a string to report an error, or undefined when valid. The resulting message is exposed through field.state.meta.errors for rendering.
Validation::Field validators.syntax: <Field validators={{ onChange: ({ value, fieldApi }) => string | undefined, onBlur: ({ value, fieldApi }) => string | undefined }} />

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The current value of the field being validated.

parameters.name: fieldApi
parameters.description: The field API supplied to the validator for field interaction and state access.

Validation::Field validators.returns: Return an error message string when the value is invalid; return undefined when it is valid.

example.title: Validate a field on change
example.explanation: The validator checks the field's current value whenever it changes. It returns a message for invalid input or undefined when the value passes; the message is then rendered from the field's error state.

useCases.title: Change-time validation
useCases.scenario: Show immediate feedback while a user edits an input.

useCases.title: Blur-time validation
useCases.scenario: Avoid showing an error until the user has finished interacting with a control.

useCases.title: Asynchronous field checks
useCases.scenario: Check a value against a remote service or other asynchronous source.

useCases.title: Inline error rendering
useCases.scenario: Display the message returned by a rule beside its input.

interview.question: What does a field validator receive and return?
interview.answer: A field-level validator is a callback supplied through a field's validation options, such as onChange or onBlur. It receives the current field value and field API, then returns an error string when invalid or undefined when valid.
interview.followUp: How would you validate only after the user leaves the field? Attach the rule to the onBlur validator instead of onChange.

interview.question: How does a validator communicate an invalid value?
interview.answer: The validator receives the current value and the field API. Returning a string records a validation error, while returning undefined indicates that the field passes this rule.
interview.followUp: Where can the rendered error be read? Use field.state.meta.errors; errorMap can distinguish which validation event produced an error.

interview.question: How do field-level and form-level validation differ?
interview.answer: Field-level rules are attached directly to each Field through callbacks such as onChange and onBlur. Form-level rules are configured through the useForm hook when validation needs broader form context.
interview.followUp: When is form-level validation preferable? Use it for rules involving multiple fields or overall form state rather than one isolated value.

keyPoints: Attach validation to a field through event-specific callbacks, including onChange and onBlur.
A validator can inspect the isolated value and use the field API while deciding whether it is valid.
Returned validation messages become available in the field's meta.errors collection for display.
Use errorMap when the UI needs to identify whether an error came from change, blur, or another validation phase.
TanStack Form supports both per-field rules and rules configured for the complete form.
Validators may run immediately or perform asynchronous work such as checking a remote API.
gotchas: Return the error text from the validator; do not throw an exception or rely on a separate error assignment.
Choose the validation callback that matches the desired timing, such as change-time or blur-time validation.

Validation::Form-level validators.sourceTitle: Form and Field Validation | TanStack Form React Docs
Validation::Form-level validators.summary: Form-level validators validate the complete form value instead of one field. Use them for cross-field rules, such as requiring password and confirmation fields to match.
Validation::Form-level validators.explanation: Form-level validators attach validation callbacks to the form rather than to individual fields. They receive the complete form value, making them suitable for cross-field rules such as comparing passwords; callbacks can run on events such as change, blur, or submit, and may be synchronous or asynchronous.
Validation::Form-level validators.syntax: useForm({ validators: { onChange, onChangeAsync, onBlur, onBlurAsync, onSubmit, onSubmitAsync, onMount, onDynamic, onDynamicAsync } })

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Form configuration containing the validators option and the form's default values and behavior.

parameters.name: argument
parameters.description: Object supplied to a validator; its value property contains the current complete form data.

Validation::Form-level validators.returns: A validator returns an error value such as a string when validation fails; it returns no error when validation succeeds. Asynchronous validators may return a promise.

example.title: Matching fields with a form-level validator
example.explanation: The form-level validator receives the complete form value, so it can compare both password fields and return an error when they differ.

useCases.title: Cross-field matching
useCases.scenario: A password and confirmation field must contain identical values.

useCases.title: Whole-form server validation
useCases.scenario: A remote endpoint checks all submitted values and reports invalid fields.

useCases.title: Schema-based form validation
useCases.scenario: One validation schema describes constraints across the complete form model.

interview.question: What is a form-level validator, and when would you use one?
interview.answer: Form-level validators are callbacks supplied through the form configuration instead of through a field. They are appropriate when validation needs access to multiple fields, and they can run at events such as change, blur, or submit.
interview.followUp: How can a form-wide server response become field errors? Use a form validator and set errors on the relevant fields; the documentation specifically describes validating all fields on submit through an asynchronous submit validator.

interview.question: How would you validate that two fields match?
interview.answer: The validator receives the current complete form value, so it can compare related properties such as password and confirmation. It returns an error when the cross-field condition fails and no error when it passes.
interview.followUp: What alternative avoids hand-written cross-field checks? Define one schema for the entire form and pass it to the form-level validators so validation errors propagate to fields.

interview.question: Can form-level validation perform asynchronous checks?
interview.answer: Form validation supports both synchronous and asynchronous checks. An asynchronous validator is useful when the rule depends on an API call, such as validating the whole form against a server during submission.
interview.followUp: Which validator event is suited to a server-wide check? Use the asynchronous submit validator, described in the documentation as a place to call one API endpoint for all fields.

keyPoints: Choose form-level validation when a rule depends on the combined state of multiple fields rather than one field alone.
In React, provide form-wide validation callbacks through the options passed to useForm.
Validation timing is configurable, including change, input, blur, and submit events.
A form validator may return immediately or await external work such as an API request.
Instead of separate callbacks, use one schema to express validation for the complete form.
gotchas: A form validator can assign errors to individual fields when a form-wide check, such as a server validation, identifies field-specific problems.
When using one schema for the entire form, its validation errors are propagated to the corresponding fields automatically.

Validation::Schema validation.sourceTitle: Form and Field Validation | TanStack Form Vue Docs
Validation::Schema validation.summary: Use a Zod or Valibot Standard Schema as a TanStack Form validator. A single form-level schema can define the complete shape while its errors flow back to the relevant fields.
Validation::Schema validation.explanation: TanStack Form accepts Standard Schema-compatible validators, including Zod and Valibot. Define one object schema for the complete form and assign it to a validator such as onChange; validation errors are then propagated to the corresponding fields.

example.title: Form-level Zod schema
example.explanation: A single Standard Schema-compatible Zod object validates the form through the form-level onChange validator.

useCases.title: Centralize form validation
useCases.scenario: A multi-field form needs one authoritative data shape and validation definition.

useCases.title: Validate individual fields
useCases.scenario: A field needs a concise, type-aware constraint from a schema library.

useCases.title: Swap schema implementations
useCases.scenario: The same validation lifecycle should work with different Standard Schema libraries.

interview.question: How does TanStack Form integrate with Zod or Valibot?
interview.answer: TanStack Form supports libraries that implement the Standard Schema specification. A complete Zod or Valibot schema can be assigned to a form-level validator, such as onChange.
interview.followUp: How would you validate only one field? Pass the schema to that field’s validators prop instead of the form-level validators.

interview.question: What is the benefit of a single form schema?
interview.answer: Create one schema for the entire form and provide it to the form-level validators configuration. The resulting errors are automatically propagated to the individual fields.
interview.followUp: Why prefer this over separate field rules? It keeps the form shape and its constraints in one schema while still displaying errors at field level.

interview.question: Where is the schema attached?
interview.answer: A schema is supplied through the validators prop in the same way as a custom validation function. For example, onChange: schema runs the schema during change validation.
interview.followUp: Can schema validation be combined with custom logic? Yes; the documentation describes combining a Standard Schema with a callback for additional control.

keyPoints: Attach a schema to either an individual field or the whole form, depending on the scope of the rules.
Schema libraries reduce handwritten validation and provide concise, type-aware rules.
A complete form schema centralizes the expected data shape and its validation rules.
Form-level schema failures are routed to the relevant fields automatically.
The integration is based on the Standard Schema interface rather than a Zod- or Valibot-specific adapter.
gotchas: Use current Zod or Valibot releases because older library versions may not implement Standard Schema.

Validation::Validation timing.sourceTitle: Form and Field Validation | TanStack Form React Docs
Validation::Validation timing.summary: Configure each validation rule to run on change, input, blur, submit, or another supported event. Use async variants and debouncing for slower checks, while invalid validation blocks submission.
Validation::Validation timing.explanation: TanStack Form attaches validators to event-specific callbacks such as onChange and onBlur, so each rule runs at the interaction point that suits it. Submission also runs these callbacks and prevents submission when the form is invalid. Async counterparts can be used for asynchronous checks, with debouncing available for expensive validation.
Validation::Validation timing.syntax: <form.Field name="field" validators={{ onChange, onBlur, onChangeAsync, onBlurAsync }} />

parameters.name: validators
parameters.description: A field validator receives the current field value and can return an error message or no error; event-specific validator names include onChange, onBlur, and async variants.

Validation::Validation timing.returns: A validator returns an error value when invalid or no error when valid; invalid validation blocks submission.

example.title: Validate at different field events
example.explanation: The email rule runs while the value changes and a second rule runs when the field loses focus; submission invokes validation before calling the submit handler.

useCases.title: Blur-based validation
useCases.scenario: Validate a field after the user leaves it to reduce interruptions.

useCases.scenario: Run server-backed or otherwise asynchronous checks with debounce.

useCases.title: Submit-time validation

keyPoints: Choose an event-specific validator—such as onChange, onBlur, or submit—to control when a rule executes.
Field-level validation is configured with callbacks on the Field component.
Use onChange when feedback should update as the user types.
Use onBlur when a rule should wait until the user leaves the field.
Use event-specific async validators for checks that need asynchronous work.
gotchas: Event-specific validators also run during submission, so submit can recheck rules even when the user has not interacted with a field recently.
An invalid result prevents the form submission handler from proceeding.
For the same event, asynchronous validation normally waits for synchronous validation to succeed.
Async validators use debouncing intervals, so their checks may not execute immediately after the triggering event.
